title: Kummer-normalized cohomological purity for a smooth divisor
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $X$ be a separated scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] that is smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ be an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] that is also smooth over $k$. Use ordinary small-etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], roots-of-unity twists [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], and $H_D^q(X,-)=H^q(R\Gamma_D(X,-))$ [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. Let $c_{D,\Lambda}:Ri_*\Lambda_D\to\Lambda_X(1)[2]$ be the positive supported Kummer map of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. The maps induced by this supported morphism are isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{pur}_{D}^{q,t}:H^{q-2}(D,\Lambda(t-1))\xrightarrow{\sim}H_D^q(X,\Lambda(t))\qquad(q,t\in\mathbf Z).$$
The composite with forgetting support is the Gysin map $i_*:H^{q-2}(D,\Lambda(t-1))\to H^q(X,\Lambda(t))$. Its normalization is $i_*(1)=+c_1(\mathcal O_X(D))$, where $c_1$ is the Kummer boundary. There is no assumption that $k$ is algebraic over a finite field.

source.place: Section 16, Theorem 16.1 for a smooth pair of codimension one and Corollary 16.2; Section 23, Direct definition of the cycle map, including its agreement with the Kummer sequence for codimension one

proof.text:
Put $N=\ell^n$. For a closed immersion $a:Z\hookrightarrow T$, write $Ra^!$ for the ordinary etale right adjoint of the exact closed direct image, as in [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. The counit triangle is [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. Its supported term represents the same support functor as in the statement: [lem-pur-divisor-relative-cone] identifies the kernel-of-restriction resolution with the signed relative cone, and [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] identifies that cone with $R\operatorname{Hom}_T(a_*\Lambda_Z,F)$. The supported-Hom normalization and its unit are explicitly supplied by [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality]. Applying the derived-Hom realization [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof] and the closed adjunction gives, naturally in bounded-below $F$,
$$H_Z^q(T,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T,\Lambda)}(a_*\Lambda_Z,F[q])=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,\Lambda)}(\Lambda_Z,Ra^!F[q]).$$
For the initial cone comparison on underlying abelian sheaves, coefficient forgetting commutes with the two derived restriction maps by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-underlying-comparison]; thus it identifies the module support kernel in the statement too. Define $\alpha_a:\Lambda_Z\to Ra^!\Lambda_T(1)[2]$ to be the adjunct of the specified $c_{Z,\Lambda}$. This defines the map to be tested, without choosing a purity isomorphism.

source.place: Section 16, restatement preceding Theorem 16.7 and its implication for 16.1; Stacks Tags 09XP and 0A45, supported sections and counit triangle

proof.text:
First take $T=\mathbf A^1_k$, $Z=\{0\}=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a=z$, and $U=\mathbf G_{m,k}$. Apply [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line] with $R=A=\Lambda$. Restriction on $H^0(-,\Lambda(1))$ is the identity, all positive affine-line cohomology vanishes, and the punctured line has only $H^1$, freely generated by $\kappa_N(t)$. The exact support sequence [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] therefore gives $H_Z^q(T,\Lambda(1))=0$ for $q\ne2$ and the isomorphism
$$\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}H_Z^2(T,\Lambda(1)),\qquad 1\longmapsto\partial\kappa_N(t).$$
Negative groups vanish since a sheaf has a nonnegative injective resolution. These are ordinary etale groups over the given $k$, with no finite-field restriction.

source.place: Section 14, Proposition 14.3; Section 16, Example 16.3 and the initial case in the proof of Theorem 16.7

proof.text: On $T=\mathbf A^1_k$ the line bundle $\mathcal O_T(Z)=(t)^\vee$ has the global frame $t^\vee$, and its divisor section is $\tau=t\,t^\vee$. Take $N=\ell^n$ and let $(\tau,E,f)$ be the data of [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary] for the supported Kummer map $c_{Z,\Lambda}$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. Then $s=f(t^\vee)\in E(T)$ lies over $1$, and on $U$ equivariance and $f(\tau)=0$ give $s|_U=f(t^{-1}\tau)=a(t^{-1})$. So $(g,m)\mapsto a(g)+ms$ kills the image of $1\mapsto(t^{-1},-1)$ on $j_!\mathbf Z_U$ and defines a map of extensions, identity on both ends, from the pushout $e_{t^{-1}}$ of [lem-per-supported-yoneda-localization] to $E$; thus $[E]=e_{t^{-1}}$. For the Kummer sequence with class $k$, that node gives that $k[1]\circ e_{t^{-1}}$ corresponds to $\partial\delta_U(t^{-1})=-\partial\kappa_N(t)$ in $H^2_Z(T,\mu_N)$, in the kernel-inclusion normalization of Step 1. For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/N$ the scalar map $\mu_N\to\Lambda(1)=\mu_N\otimes\Lambda$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is an isomorphism, and scalar forgetting commutes with the section maps [lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-underlying-comparison]. Hence under Step 1 $c_{Z,\Lambda}$ is $-\partial\kappa_N(t)$, a generator of $H^2_Z(T,\Lambda(1))\cong\Lambda$ by Step 2; only that it is a generator is used below. On $\operatorname{Spec}k$ sections are the identity geometric stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant], hence exact and conservative, including for module sheaves by forgetting scalars. The cohomology of $Rz^!\Lambda_T(1)[2]$ is therefore $\Lambda$ in degree zero and zero otherwise; $\alpha_z$ sends $1$ to this generator in degree zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], $\alpha_z$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Section 16, local model and Section 23, direct cycle map in codimension one; signed relative calculation as in the cited torsor lemma

proof.text: Fix $x\in D$. By [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] there are an open $V\subset X$ containing $x$ and an etale map $h:V\to\mathbf A_k^{a+b}$ for which $E=D\times_XV$ is cut out by the last $b$ coordinates, a regular sequence. In the local ring at $x$, their classes form a basis of $(I/I^2)\otimes\kappa(x)$ by the degree-one clause of [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial]. On the other hand $I=(f)$ with $f$ a nonzerodivisor since $D$ is Cartier. The map $R/(f)\to(f)/(f^2)$ sending $\bar r\mapsto rf$ is bijective: surjectivity is immediate and $rf\in(f^2)$ implies $r\in(f)$ by cancellation of $f$. Thus that same fibre has dimension one and $b=1$. In particular $E$ is the scheme-theoretic inverse image of $0$ under the last-coordinate map $v:V\to\mathbf A^1_k$. This map is smooth: the coordinate projection $\mathbf A_k^{a+1}=\mathbf A^a_{\mathbf A^1_k}\to\mathbf A^1_k$ is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and composition with the etale $h$ is smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence].

source.place: Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, specialized to a Cartier ideal; Milne Section 16, Lemma 16.8

proof.text:
Pull the counit triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] for $(\mathbf A^1_k,0,\Lambda(1))$ back by this smooth $v$. Compare it with the counit triangle for $(V,E,v^*\Lambda(1))$. The middle comparison is the identity. The third is the actual open direct-image exchange and is an isomorphism by [sbc-thm-bounded-derived-smooth-base-change]: the open $\mathbf G_m\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and its finite locally constant input $\Lambda(1)$ is bounded constructible by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The second square commutes, the exchange being the mate of the open units, so the axioms of [def-weil-triangulated-category] complete the identity and the exchange to a morphism of triangles. Its long cohomology sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], with their connecting maps, and the five-lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] make its first component invertible in every degree, hence invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. Its composite with the counit of $(V,E)$ is the pulled-back counit; as its source is of the form $e_*(-)$ (below), composing with that counit is bijective on such maps, so this component is the canonical comparison. More explicitly, writing $e:E\hookrightarrow V$ and $v_E:E\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, it is
$$v^*z_*Rz^!\Lambda(1)\longrightarrow e_*Re^!v^*\Lambda(1).$$
The closed direct-image comparison on its source is invertible by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange], in module coefficients by the conservative exchange comparison [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison]; the closed counit $e^*e_*\cong1$ is [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. Apply $e^*$ to conclude that $v_E^*Rz^!\Lambda(1)\to Re^!\Lambda_V(1)$ is invertible. This three-term triangle argument uses smooth base change for an open direct image, not any purity theorem.

source.place: Tag 0A45, lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle, and Tag 0F09, lemma-smooth-base-change-general, constant inverse system; two-out-of-three for the counit triangles

proof.text: The first comparison in Step 5 is the map whose composite with the supported counit is the pullback of the original supported counit. Therefore it sends the adjunct of $v^*c_{Z,\Lambda}$ to the adjunct of $c_{E,\Lambda}$: after applying $e_*$ and then its counit, both composites are $v^*c_{Z,\Lambda}$. Equality follows from the adjunction bijection. Here the equality $v^*c_{Z,\Lambda}=c_{E,\Lambda}$, with the closed exchange inserted, is exactly the Cartier-preserving pullback clause of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]; the pullback divisor $E$ is Cartier by Step 4. Hence $\alpha_e$ is the composite of the pullback of the isomorphism $\alpha_z$ and the isomorphism of Step 5, so is invertible. Apply the same triangle comparison to the open inclusion $V\hookrightarrow X$: open direct image commutes with this etale restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-localization-exchange], with the actual module mate identified by [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison]. It identifies $\alpha_e$ with the restriction of $\alpha_i$ to $E$. These $E$ cover $D$. Exact geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and their conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], together with the derived cohomology criterion, now imply that $\alpha_i:\Lambda_D\to Ri^!\Lambda_X(1)[2]$ is an isomorphism globally.

source.place: Section 16, proof of Theorem 16.7: etale locality after defining the map; Stacks Tag 0A45 counit triangle and its adjunction maps

proof.text:
For $L=\Lambda_X(t-1)$, [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] gives its inverse $L^\vee$ and $i^*L=\Lambda_D(t-1)$. The projection isomorphism for the closed immersion is [lem-sf-etale-generic-immersion-projection]. Its adjoint conjugate gives the twist comparison, as can be seen directly from
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,Ri^!(K\otimes L))=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,K\otimes L)=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*(P\otimes i^*L^\vee),K)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,Ri^!K\otimes i^*L).$$
The equalities use tensoring by the inverse line and the two adjunctions; naturality identifies the resulting map with the adjunct of the twisted $c_{D,\Lambda}$. Thus tensoring $\alpha_i$ by $\Lambda_D(t-1)$ and shifting by $-2$ gives the isomorphism $\Lambda_D(t-1)[-2]\to Ri^!\Lambda_X(t)$. Apply the last Hom functor of Step 1, or its injective-resolution global-sections realization [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof], in degree $q$. This gives precisely
$$H^{q-2}(D,\Lambda(t-1))\xrightarrow{\sim}H_D^q(X,\Lambda(t))$$
induced by the specified supported morphism, for every integer $q,t$. For $q<0$ both groups are zero; no cohomological bound on $\dim X$ is needed.

source.place: Section 16, Theorem 16.7 implies Theorem 16.1, with the invertible roots-of-unity twists of Section 16, first page

proof.text: The supported term in [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] maps to ordinary cohomology by its counit; [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality] identifies forgetting support with precomposition with $u_D:\Lambda_X\to i_*\Lambda_D$. Accordingly forgetting support after the isomorphism of Step 7 is exactly the Gysin map, the map induced by the twisted supported $c_{D,\Lambda}$ into ordinary cohomology. For $q=2,t=1$, the section $1\in H^0(D,\Lambda)$ is the map $u_D$ under that identification. The equation in [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] is $c_{D,\Lambda}u_D=c_1(\mathcal O_X(D))$. It proves $i_*(1)=+c_1(\mathcal O_X(D))$ with the Kummer-boundary sign. The argument also covers $D=\varnothing$ (the supported object and divisor class are both zero) and disconnected smooth schemes, since all comparisons were local along $D$.

source.place: Section 16, Corollary 16.2, and Section 23, Direct definition of the cycle map, final codimension-one sentence

proof_origin.place: Section 16, Theorems 16.1 and 16.7 and Lemma 16.8; Section 23, codimension-one cycle class.
